_comment: AUTHORITATIVE SOURCE REGISTRY - the source of record per subject, and the only web reach the platform has. Three things depend on this file: (1) the delivery Function's outbound allow-list (functions/delivery/urlpolicy.py regenerates its DEFAULT_ALLOWLIST from the 'domains' below - run scripts/sync_url_allowlist.py, checked by scripts/check_knowledge_sources.py in CI); (2) the agents' citation discipline (knowledge pack agents/knowledge-packs/authoritative-sources.md, attached to every agent that makes a regulatory, control or vulnerability statement); (3) what an 'api:' access mode means - a registered read-only connection in integrations/registry.json, attached like any other tool. TIERS: 1 = the authority itself (cite it and nothing else where it speaks); 2 = official or standard-body material that interprets or implements tier 1; 3 = a commercial or observational signal that may point at something but evidences nothing on its own. A deliverable NEVER rests a conclusion on a tier-3 source. EGRESS RULE (governance/DATA_PROTECTION_GUARDRAILS.md section 1) is unchanged by this file and applies to every entry: only public terms leave - a CVE id, a CELEX number, a public product name, a supplier's own public domain when the engagement is not confidential. Never an ENX identifier, an assessment id, a person, or document content. Adding a source here is a Tier-B change (operations/CHANGE_MANAGEMENT.md): it widens the outbound allow-list.

_access_modes.api:<connection>: a registered read-only connection in integrations/registry.json - structured, citable, rate-limited
_access_modes.page:osint-proxy: sanitised public page fetch through the delivery Function (GET /api/fetch_public_page) - allow-listed host, outbound DLP on the URL, size cap, audited
_access_modes.search:web-search: Bing grounding on PUBLIC terms, to FIND a tier-1 or tier-2 page; the finding is then read through osint-proxy and cited from there, never from the search snippet

precedence: The authority that made the rule outranks anyone describing it: EUR-Lex over a law-firm briefing, the ESAs over a vendor webinar, NVD/CVE over a blog, IAF CertSearch over a certificate PDF, the supplier's own advisory over press coverage of it.
A consolidated EU text outranks the original act when advising on the law in force - and the consolidation date is stated.
A final report outranks a consultation paper; a consultation paper is never presented as settled.
Where two tier-1 sources genuinely conflict, both are reported with their dates and the conflict is named - it is not resolved silently.
No source of any tier justifies asserting a date, an article number or a score that was not actually read in this run.

sources.name: EUR-Lex / CELLAR (Publications Office of the EU)
sources.authority: Publications Office of the European Union
covers: every RTS/ITS published in the Official Journal
sources.use_for: The authentic text and the legal metadata of any EU instrument: article wording, entry into force, date of application, amendments, consolidations, in-force status.
sources.citation: Instrument, article/paragraph, CELEX (consolidated CELEX and its consolidation date where a consolidation was read), retrieval date.
sources.refresh: on every use - the law in force is a point-in-time fact
sources._comment: The source of record for EU law on this platform. A regulatory statement in a deliverable cites a CELEX, never a secondary summary.

sources.name: European Commission
covers: AI Act guidelines and the AI Pact
sources.use_for: Commission-level interpretation, guidelines, adequacy decisions and the status of acts not yet in the Official Journal.
sources.citation: Body, document title, reference, publication date, URL, retrieved date.

sources.name: National transposition and supervisory sources
sources.authority: Member State legislators and competent authorities
sources.use_for: Where an EU directive only binds through national law - NIS2 above all - the obligation that actually applies to an ENX entity is the national transposition, in its own language.
sources.citation: Instrument in the national language, article, official gazette reference, date, URL, retrieved date.
sources.refresh: when the entity scope or a transposition deadline is in question
sources._comment: Euronext operates in several Member States: a NIS2 answer that cites only the Directive is incomplete for an entity-level question.

sources.name: ESAs - EBA, ESMA, EIOPA (and the Joint Committee)
covers: DORA RTS/ITS and the Register of Information templates
oversight of critical ICT third-party providers
sources.use_for: The supervisory expectation that sits between the Regulation and practice: final report vs consultation paper, and which applies when.
sources.citation: Authority, document type (final report / consultation paper / guidelines), reference number, date, URL, retrieved date, and whether it is final.
sources._comment: A consultation paper is never cited as settled expectation - the change watch marks it MEDIUM or LOW confidence.

sources.name: European Data Protection Board (and EDPS)
sources.use_for: Authoritative interpretation of the GDPR for processor contracts, transfers, DPIAs and breach notification.
sources.citation: EDPB Guidelines <n>/<year>, version, adoption date, paragraph, URL.
sources.refresh: quarterly and on any transfer question

sources.name: ENISA - EU Agency for Cybersecurity
sources.use_for: Technical measures and threat context behind NIS2 Art. 21, and the state of EU certification schemes a supplier may claim.
sources.citation: ENISA, report title, version, publication date, URL, retrieved date.

sources.name: CERT-EU and national CSIRTs
sources.use_for: European advisory context for a supplier incident or a vulnerability affecting a service Euronext consumes.
sources.citation: Issuing CSIRT, advisory reference, date, URL, retrieved date.

sources.name: ISO / IEC
sources.use_for: Scope, edition, publication date, clause and control NUMBERING of record - and whether an amendment (e.g. 27001:2022/Amd 1:2024) applies.
sources.citation: ISO/IEC <number>:<year>[/Amd], clause or control id, edition date. Standard TEXT is licensed - quote only what Euronext's licensed copy permits and cite the clause, never paste the standard.
sources.refresh: annually and on a known revision
sources._comment: THIRD_PARTY_IP.md governs reproduction: the platform reasons from clause numbers and Euronext's licensed copies, never from a pirated full text.

sources.name: NIST
sources.authority: National Institute of Standards and Technology
sources.use_for: Control catalogues and framework functions/categories, free to quote, used for mapping and for controls language.
sources.citation: NIST, publication id and revision, section or control id, publication date, URL.

sources.name: Center for Internet Security
sources.use_for: Safeguard-level control detail and implementation groups, and benchmark hardening expectations for a platform a supplier runs.
sources.citation: CIS Controls v8.1, control and safeguard number, IG level, version date.

sources.name: Cloud Security Alliance
sources.use_for: Cloud control mapping and the STAR registry entry (level, scope, date) a supplier's CAIQ claim must match.
sources.citation: CSA CCM version, control id; STAR registry entry with level and date.

sources.name: OWASP / PTES / FIRST CVSS
sources.use_for: Methodology adequacy of a penetration test, and the CVSS calculation of record when a tester's score has to be checked.
sources.citation: Standard, version, section; for CVSS the full vector string and version.

sources.name: PCI Security Standards Council
sources.use_for: What a supplier's AoC actually attests, and the v4 requirements that fall on a third-party service provider.
sources.citation: PCI DSS version, requirement number, document date.

sources.name: AICPA
sources.authority: American Institute of Certified Public Accountants
sources.use_for: What a SOC report type can and cannot support, and the TSC in scope.
sources.citation: AICPA TSC year, criterion id; SSAE/ISAE standard number.

sources.name: IAASB
sources.authority: International Auditing and Assurance Standards Board
sources.use_for: The European equivalent assurance standards a supplier's report is issued under, and what the opinion covers.
sources.citation: ISAE standard number and paragraph, issue date.

sources.name: IAF CertSearch
sources.use_for: Independent confirmation that a certificate a supplier presented is real, accredited, in force and scoped to the service.
sources.citation: IAF CertSearch entry, certificate number, certification body, scope, valid-to date, retrieval date.
sources.refresh: on every certificate accepted as evidence
sources._comment: A certificate PDF is a claim; the registry entry is the verification.

sources.name: National accreditation bodies (EA members)
covers: accreditation status of a certification body
sources.use_for: Whether the body that issued a certificate is itself accredited for that scheme - the step most evidence reviews skip.
sources.citation: Accreditation body, certificate body reference, scheme, status, date.
sources.refresh: when a certification body is unfamiliar

sources.name: Official company registers
sources.authority: National registries and the EU Business Registers portal
sources.use_for: The legal entity behind the trading name, its LEI for the DORA Register of Information, and its group structure for concentration analysis.
sources.citation: Register, entity name, registration number or LEI, retrieval date.
sources.refresh: on intake and on register build

sources.name: NIST National Vulnerability Database
sources.use_for: The published severity of record for any CVE named in a pentest, vulnerability report or supplier advisory.
sources.citation: CVE id, CVSS vector and version, NVD lastModified date.

sources.name: CVE Program (MITRE)
sources.use_for: The record itself when NVD enrichment lags, and the CNA's own statement.
sources.citation: CVE id, CNA, record version and date.
sources.refresh: when NVD has no enrichment yet

sources.name: CISA Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalogue
sources.use_for: The citable fact that changes priority: this vulnerability is being exploited now.
sources.citation: CISA KEV, CVE id, dateAdded, dueDate, catalogue version read.

sources.name: FIRST EPSS
sources.use_for: Likelihood of exploitation in the next 30 days, to order remediation sensibly alongside CVSS and KEV.
sources.citation: EPSS score and percentile WITH the date read (scores move daily).

sources.name: MITRE ATT&CK and D3FEND
sources.use_for: Technique-level language for incident analysis and for describing what a control actually stops.
sources.citation: ATT&CK technique id and name, matrix version.

sources.name: Supplier and platform security advisories
sources.use_for: What the supplier says about its own incident or vulnerability - the primary source for a supplier incident assessment.
sources.citation: Vendor, advisory id, version, publication and last-update timestamps.
sources.refresh: on incident and on evidence review
sources._comment: The supplier domain is allow-listed per call (supplierDomain parameter), not kept in the standing list.

sources.name: Supplier trust centres and sub-processor lists
sources.use_for: The fourth-party chain and the data-location claims that the concentration analysis and the Register of Information depend on.
sources.citation: Page title, URL, retrieved date, and the version/effective date the page itself states.
sources.refresh: on intake, on register build, on concentration

sources.name: SecurityScorecard
sources.use_for: External posture signal and rating drift for the monitoring radar.
sources.citation: Provider, score and factor, observation date.
sources._comment: Tier 3: a commercial signal, never a finding on its own - it points at something to verify, it does not evidence it.

sources.name: Public TLS / certificate observatories
sources.use_for: Passive, public confirmation of a supplier's externally observable configuration - no scanning, no probing.
sources.citation: Tool, target host, observation timestamp.
sources._comment: Passive observation only: ActiveScanningAllowed is No on this platform.
